headline: US-Iran conflict escalates with American troops killed in Jordan, sending oil surging 3.6% — meanwhile GOOG earnings land Tuesday US time and your AI ETF took a 5% hit today.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: Biggest mover today, down 5% at the ASX close. The AI ETF tracks global AI-focused stocks, and last night's broad NASDAQ sell-off (down 1.4%) dragged the whole sector lower. No company-specific bad news — this is broader tech sentiment weakness ahead of a heavy US earnings week.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: Down 3.1% today, the second-worst performer in the portfolio. Emerging markets are getting squeezed by rising oil prices (up 3.6%), which pushes up costs across developing economies, and ongoing geopolitical jitters around Iran. The Aussie dollar holding relatively steady didn't provide much buffer.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara dropped 3.1% today. Lithium prices remain under pressure globally — analysts note mixed signals on demand, with EV uptake growing but lithium supply still outpacing it. The stock is now down 35.8% on your total investment — a tough run, but the long-term electrification story hasn't gone away.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: GOOG fell 2.2% last night in a pre-earnings pullback — earnings are due Tuesday 22 July (US time). Google Cloud just hit $20B in quarterly revenue and analysts are watching whether AI is converting into real profit. The dip looks like nerves ahead of results rather than anything structural.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft slipped 1.8% last night alongside the broader NASDAQ decline. The company is spending $190B on AI infrastructure in 2026 — that's a massive bet — and earnings are coming soon too. BNP Paribas analysts expect revenue and spending to both accelerate. Short-term softness, long-term story intact.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two dipped 1.2% last night, largely moving with the broader market. The positive news: the CEO reconfirmed the GTA 6 release date with the SEC this week, which is a meaningful commitment. The long-term case here is all about GTA 6 — and that timeline is holding.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: Down 1.1% today, tracking last night's S&P 500 fall of 1%. This ETF mirrors the entire US share market, so when Wall Street has a rough session — driven by Iran conflict fears and pre-earnings nerves — VTS follows. Nothing specific to worry about here.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: The most diversified holding in the portfolio, VDHG slipped just 0.9% today — the most resilient performer on a down day. Its mix of Australian, international and bond assets provides a natural cushion when any one market sells off. Exactly what it's designed to do.

watch_today.title: GOOG earnings Tuesday — big moment for your holding
watch_today.detail: Alphabet reports earnings on Tuesday 22 July (US time, so Wednesday morning AEST). Google Cloud just hit $20B in quarterly revenue and the market wants to see AI turning into real profit. The stock has dropped about 4% in the lead-up — classic pre-earnings nerves. For a long-term holder, sit tight and see the numbers. No reason to sell before earnings.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX — down 5% today, but don't panic
watch_today.detail: Your AI ETF took the biggest hit in the portfolio today, falling 5% at the ASX close. This tracks the NASDAQ sell-off from last night and general tech jitters ahead of big US earnings. The long-term AI investment thesis is very much intact — if anything, this kind of dip could be worth watching as a potential top-up opportunity for a long-term believer in AI.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — holding through a tough stretch
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals is now down 35.8% on your total investment and dropped another 3.1% today. Lithium prices remain soft globally, but the long-term demand case — EVs, batteries, energy storage — is still real. This is painful to hold, but selling now would lock in the loss. The thesis is bruised, not broken. Sit tight unless you see a fundamental change in the lithium outlook.

watch_today.title: Oil surging on US-Iran conflict — watch the flow-on
watch_today.detail: Crude oil jumped 3.6% last night to $81.78/barrel as the US-Iran conflict escalated — two US troops were killed in Jordan, the US launched new airstrikes, and Iran hit Gulf allies in retaliation. Higher oil means higher inflation pressure globally, which can push interest rates up — bad news for growth stocks and your US-heavy holdings. Worth watching how this develops this week.

watch_today.title: VGE.AX — emerging markets bearing the brunt
watch_today.detail: Your Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF fell 3.1% today — the sharpest ASX-listed drop in the portfolio. Rising oil hurts energy-importing emerging economies, and Middle East tensions add geopolitical risk. The long-term diversification case for VGE is solid, but expect continued volatility while the Iran situation plays out.

watch_today.title: MSFT earnings also approaching — keep an eye out
watch_today.detail: Microsoft earnings are coming in the next week or two (US time). The company is spending $190B on AI infrastructure this year — a massive bet — and analysts at BNP Paribas expect both revenue and spending to accelerate. The stock is down 11% on your total investment, but the long-term AI infrastructure story is one of the strongest in global tech. Hold and watch the earnings print.

world.summary: The US-Iran conflict has escalated sharply this week, with American troops killed in Jordan and retaliatory airstrikes flying in both directions. Meanwhile Trump's election fraud claims remain in the spotlight after newly declassified documents failed to back them up, and the Trump-Xi relationship is taking a curious turn.

stories.title: Two US Troops Killed in Jordan as US-Iran Conflict Enters Seventh Day
stories.why_it_matters: Two US soldiers were killed and one is missing after Iranian-linked attacks in Jordan, marking a major escalation in the week-long US-Iran conflict. The US responded by launching fresh airstrikes, targeting bridges and water plants inside Iran — now into a seventh consecutive day of strikes. Iran hit back by targeting US allies in Gulf states. This is the most serious direct US-Iran military confrontation in years and is why oil jumped 3.6% overnight — markets are pricing in real supply disruption risk if the conflict spreads to key shipping routes in the region.

stories.title: Trump's Declassified Documents Don't Back His Election Fraud Claims
stories.why_it_matters: Trump gave a major address claiming newly declassified documents prove Chinese interference in the 2020 election and justify his ongoing claims of fraud. Fact-checkers at PBS, NBC News and The Guardian have reviewed the documents and found they offer little to no evidence for those claims — the documents mostly show routine intelligence assessments, not a coordinated Chinese plot to steal the election. The speech is part of Trump's continued effort to relitigate 2020, but the substance doesn't hold up to scrutiny according to multiple independent reviews.

stories.title: Trump Pursuing Closer Bond With Xi Despite Hostile Rhetoric
stories.why_it_matters: Despite making a high-profile speech accusing China of election interference, Trump is simultaneously working behind the scenes to deepen his personal relationship with Chinese President Xi Jinping, according to the New York Times. The two leaders are reportedly in regular contact, and Trump's team is seeking trade and economic arrangements. This kind of mixed messaging — publicly hostile, privately conciliatory — creates real uncertainty for global markets and trade policy, which affects everything from Australian exports to the value of your US-listed stocks.

stories.title: Iran Renews Attacks on Gulf States After Latest Night of US Strikes
stories.why_it_matters: Iran has escalated further by striking US allies across the Gulf — including infrastructure targets — after the latest round of US airstrikes. This tit-for-tat cycle is now well into its second week with no sign of a ceasefire or diplomatic off-ramp. The risk for everyday Australians: sustained conflict in this region pushes up fuel prices globally, which feeds into petrol prices at the bowser and higher inflation across the board. Gold is also rising (up 0.8% to $4,018/oz) as investors seek safety.

markets.summary: A rough night on Wall Street last night as Iran tensions and pre-earnings nerves hit tech stocks hard. The NASDAQ dropped 1.4% and the S&P 500 fell 1%. Closer to home, the ASX 200 closed down 0.5% today. The big story in commodities: oil jumped 3.6% on the Middle East escalation, and gold climbed to over $4,000/oz.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Closed down 0.5% today, tracking last night's Wall Street weakness and Iran jitters.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Fell 1% last night — pre-earnings caution and escalating Middle East conflict weighed on sentiment.

indicators.name: NASDAQ
indicators.note: Tech bore the brunt last night, down 1.4%, dragging AI and growth stocks lower ahead of big earnings.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Surged 3.6% last night — the US-Iran conflict is the driver, with markets pricing in supply disruption risk.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold topped $4,000/oz again — investors are buying the safe haven as geopolitical risk rises.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar edged slightly lower against the USD, sitting just below 70 cents.

politics.summary: The Albanese government has released its formal response to a parliamentary report on Islamophobia in Australia, but has stopped short of one of the key recommendations — drawing criticism from advocates.

stories.title: Government Responds to Islamophobia Report, But Stops Short on Terror Laws
stories.why_it_matters: The Albanese government has responded to a parliamentary report on Islamophobia in Australia, acknowledging it is 'dangerously close to becoming normalised.' However, the government stopped short of removing 'religious motivation' as a factor in terrorism laws — a key recommendation from the report. Advocates and community groups had pushed for this change, arguing the current framing unfairly targets Muslim Australians. The government's decision to hold back on that specific change is being seen as a political compromise, balancing community concerns against security agency preferences. The broader response signals Labor is taking the issue seriously, even if not going as far as some had hoped.

ai.summary: A big week in AI: China's DeepSeek has released a new model (V4) that's being compared to ChatGPT and Claude, reigniting the debate about whether the US is falling behind in the AI race. Meanwhile, millions of Chinese users are being forced to end AI 'relationships' after a government crackdown.

stories.title: DeepSeek V4 Arrives — How Does It Stack Up Against ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude?
stories.why_it_matters: China's DeepSeek has dropped its V4 model, which is being benchmarked directly against ChatGPT (OpenAI), Claude (Anthropic) and Gemini (Google). Early comparisons suggest it's competitive on reasoning and coding tasks, and it's raising fresh questions about whether US AI companies are losing their edge. For your GOOG holding specifically, every strong Chinese AI model release adds competitive pressure to Google's Gemini — something to keep in mind heading into earnings.

stories.title: US 'Tying Itself in Knots' Over AI as China Releases New Model — David Sacks
stories.why_it_matters: David Sacks, the White House's AI and crypto czar, has publicly argued that the US is getting in its own way on AI by layering on too many regulations — just as China drops a new competitive model. His argument: while American companies navigate a complex web of rules, Chinese firms are shipping products. This is a real policy tension: too little regulation risks harm, too much risks falling behind. For investors in AI stocks, the regulatory environment is a key risk to watch.

stories.title: Millions of Chinese Forced to End AI 'Relationships' After Government Crackdown
stories.why_it_matters: Millions of Chinese users have been forced to cut off AI chatbot 'relationships' — emotional bonds with AI companions — after Beijing ordered platforms to restrict or shut down these services. Users described distress and grief ('my heart is empty') at losing what had become meaningful daily interactions. China's government is concerned about people forming deep emotional dependencies on AI, and the crackdown is one of the most striking examples yet of how governments are trying to manage the social effects of AI. It also shows the commercial risk for AI companion apps globally — regulation can kill an entire product category overnight.

stories.title: Peter Thiel's 'Antichrist' Theory of AI Regulation Goes Public
stories.why_it_matters: Tech billionaire and Trump ally Peter Thiel has publicly shared what Fortune calls his 'Antichrist' theory — the idea that climate and tech regulators represent a kind of existential threat to human progress, and that AI should be left almost entirely free from government oversight. Thiel is highly influential in Silicon Valley and among Republican policymakers, so his framing matters for how AI regulation gets shaped in the US. It's a stark contrast to the EU's heavy-handed approach, and it puts the spotlight on a fundamental question: who gets to decide how powerful AI systems are governed?

sport.summary: A massive Round 20 in the NRL wrapping up this weekend on the Gold Coast, with the local Titans pulling off a thriller against Manly at Cbus Super Stadium. The Bulldogs and Raiders kept their finals dreams alive, while the Tigers had a nightmare week. In AFL, Tom Lynch hit 500 career goals.

stories.title: Titans Stun Sea Eagles 38-32 in Gold Coast Thriller
stories.why_it_matters: Your Gold Coast Titans delivered a belter at Cbus Super Stadium this afternoon, beating Manly Sea Eagles 38-32. Fox Sports described it as a 'devastating double blow' to Manly's finals push under coach Kieran Foran. A high-scoring, back-and-forth game — great result for the home side.

stories.title: Tigers Get Flogged 32-0 by Bulldogs, Then Two Stars Handed Bans
stories.why_it_matters: The Wests Tigers had a horror Saturday — thrashed 32-0 by the Bulldogs at Accor Stadium, then had two key players handed suspension bans after the match. A brutal double blow for a club already well out of finals contention. Meanwhile the Bulldogs kept their own finals dream alive with the big win.

stories.title: Warriors Eye Minor Premiership After Scraping Past Dragons
stories.why_it_matters: The New Zealand Warriors had to survive a scare against the Dragons, winning 20-12 in a game that was closer than the score suggests — the Dragons fumed over refereeing decisions after the game. But the Warriors got it done, and with the result they're now eyeing the minor premiership (finishing top of the ladder) heading into the back end of the season.

stories.title: Dolphins Demolish Cowboys 36-16 at Suncorp
stories.why_it_matters: The Dolphins put on a show at Suncorp Stadium today, belting the Cowboys 36-16 in a statement performance. A dominant result that keeps the Dolphins firmly in the finals mix heading into the pointy end of the season.

stories.title: Tom Lynch Kicks Career Goal 500 in AFL Milestone
stories.why_it_matters: Richmond's Tom Lynch reached 500 career AFL goals this weekend — a rare milestone in the game and a personal moment a long time coming for the veteran forward. Lynch has had an injury-interrupted career, making the achievement all the more meaningful.
